response: Normally sighted and visually impaired pedestrians can make accurate and reliable street crossing decisions. However, when relying solely on auditory information, all pedestrians, regardless of their visual ability, tend to overestimate the time available to cross the street. Blind pedestrians, in particular, may face challenges in making street crossing decisions, especially when using auditory information only, and may benefit from training to improve their detection and interpretation of vehicular gap times. Overall, while normally sighted and visually impaired pedestrians can make reliable decisions, blind pedestrians may require additional support or training to ensure their safety when crossing streets.
